claim: Land within 50 m of a lakeshore is State public property, measured from the furthest line reached by water in successive floods (Art 2); 10 m for big rivers, 5 m for small rivers on the annexed list, 2 m for other rivers (Art 3); protected area; no activities or buildings allowed except lake/river protection works or activities authorised by the Minister in charge of environment after a prior EIA (Art 4); natural vegetation reserved, artificial vegetation only to restore damaged land or control erosion (Art 5); dumping solid or liquid waste prohibited (Art 6).
title: Ministerial Order N°007/16.01 of 15/07/2010 determining the length of land on shores of lakes and rivers transferred to public property (Official Gazette n° 37 of 13/09/2010)
organization: Ministry of Environment and Lands (MINIRENA), Republic of Rwanda
notes: Trilingual gazette text read in full from a mirror. REMA also lists this order on its Ministerial Orders page (LOC-11). Older than 5 years; no repeal found in this research but not confirmed [U]. Law 27/2021 Art 31(2) refers to an Order of the Minister for the width.

claim: Art 42(5): building an agricultural or livestock installation within 10 m of stream/river banks or 50 m of lake banks is prohibited; Art 42(6): cattle kraal, slaughter house or cattle market within 60 m of streams/rivers or 200 m of lake banks prohibited; Art 42(7): building in water sources, streams, rivers, lakes and the buffer zone within 10 m of streams or 50 m of lakes prohibited; Art 42(10): building in a swamp or within 20 m of the swamp boundary prohibited; Art 42(11)-(12): draining swamps or draining/diverting/blocking rivers without authorisation prohibited; Art 49: fine FRW 500,000 and demolition for kraal/slaughterhouse/market, agricultural-livestock installation, swamp-buffer building or waste dumping within the distances; Art 30: list of projects needing an EIA is set by Ministerial Order.
title: Law N°48/2018 of 13/08/2018 on Environment (Official Gazette n° Special of 21/09/2018)
organization: Parliament of the Republic of Rwanda (Official Gazette)
notes: Trilingual gazette text read from a third-party copy. The text says 'agricultural and livestock installation' (not cultivation or grazing); press reports (LOC-09) describe farming and grazing as barred in the buffer, so the exact reach for crops and grazing is [U].

claim: State owns and controls water resources (Art 18); allocation priority is domestic needs, then environmental protection, then economic activities (Art 19); water use and installations that may modify flow, level or quality need a water use permit listed by Ministerial Order (Art 21); permit fees set by Ministerial Order (Art 22); using water or carrying out a water-related activity without a required permit is an offence: 2 to 3 months' imprisonment and/or a FRW 500,000 fine (Art 36).
title: Law N°49/2018 of 13/08/2018 determining the use and management of water resources in Rwanda (Official Gazette n° Special of 21/09/2018)
organization: Parliament of the Republic of Rwanda (Official Gazette)
notes: Trilingual gazette text read from a mirror.

claim: A water resources use permit is required before: irrigation of more than one hectare; infrastructure in rivers or lakes; construction of a dam; fish farming in a lake or artificial pond; domestic water supply, water supply for livestock (farms) and community settlements; coffee washing stations; industrial use; recreation requiring water (Art 3). Application through the District Mayor with a non-refundable FRW 35,000 fee paid to FONERWA (Art 4). Irrigation above 10 ha, infrastructure in rivers/lakes and dams also need an EIA certificate and a feasibility study; farm/domestic supply needs a feasibility study (Art 5). Decision within 90 days (Art 7); online application (Art 9); initial validity up to 15 years, renewable (Art 11); meters required for domestic supply, hydropower and irrigation above 10 ha, and an annual use report (Art 12).
title: Ministerial Order N°001/MoE/24 of 02/04/2024 relating to water resources use permit (Official Gazette n° Special of 03/04/2024)
organization: Ministry of Environment, Republic of Rwanda
notes: Full trilingual text read from FAOLEX. FAOLEX record (https://leap.unep.org/en/countries/rw/national-legislation/ministerial-order-no-001moe24-relating-water-resources-use-permit) says it repeals Ministerial Order Nº002/16.01 of 24/05/2013. No volume threshold for livestock or domestic supply appears in the text [U].

claim: Annex 1 (full ESIA) lists, among others: agricultural activities using chemical fertilisers or pesticides in a wetland; large-scale agricultural activities using chemical fertilisers or pesticides outdoors ('large-scale' is not defined); construction of artificial lakes; construction of water storage dams; marshland reclamation; slaughter houses; warehouses for perishable agricultural commodities of half a hectare or more. Annex 2 (partial ESIA) includes coffee washing stations. No licence or permit may be issued without an ESIA approval certificate (Art 4); the Authority may require an ESIA for an unlisted project with a similar, irreversible impact (Art 5(2)); terms of reference approved within 14 days (Art 7(5)); decision within 20 working days (Art 12(2)).
title: Ministerial Order N°003/MoE/25 of 19/08/2025 relating to environmental and social impact assessment (Official Gazette n° Special of 20/08/2025)
organization: Ministry of Environment, Republic of Rwanda
notes: Full trilingual text read from the RDB business-procedures site. Replaces the 2019 EIA order per press coverage (https://allafrica.com/stories/202509010044.html, not opened). Ordinary crop and livestock farming of 2-10 ha is not itself listed.

claim: Protected swampland: no activity allowed except research or science. Unprotected swampland: agriculture, fish farming, recreation, tourism, quarrying, research, energy and other approved activities may be carried out under a concession from the Ministry in charge of land, with infrastructure subject to prior environmental impact assessment (Arts 2, 5); the annex lists swamplands and their classification.
title: Prime Minister's Order N°001/03 of 30/01/2024 relating to swamplands (Official Gazette n° Special of 31/01/2024)
organization: Prime Minister's Office, Republic of Rwanda (published by REMA)
notes: Articles 1-5 read; the annex list of swamplands (by district) was not searched for the candidate zones [U]. The text contains no buffer width; the 20 m swamp buffer is in Law 48/2018 Art 42(10).

claim: Rwandans are entitled to freehold; a Presidential Order may grant freehold to a foreigner only in exceptional strategic national interest; private freehold land is limited to 2 ha per person unless a Ministerial Order authorises otherwise (Art 6). Tenure is by emphyteutic lease or freehold (Art 9). Lease and concession periods do not exceed 99 years, renewable; automatic renewal applies to Rwandans (Art 10). A State land concession cannot exceed 49 years (Art 11). A foreigner has the right to an emphyteutic lease or a land concession, allocated only for investment (Art 16). 'Foreigner' includes an individual without Rwandan nationality and a company, international organisation or cooperative with foreign legal personality (Art 2(30)). Lands on the banks of lakes or rivers up to a distance set by Ministerial Order, measured from the furthest line reached by water in successive floods excluding exceptional floods, are State public domain (Art 31(2)).
title: Law N°27/2021 of 10/06/2021 governing land (Official Gazette n° Special of 10/06/2021)
organization: Parliament of the Republic of Rwanda (Official Gazette)
notes: Trilingual text read from FAOLEX (articles quoted above read directly). Lease terms for specific uses are set by a Prime Minister's Order not read here [U].

claim: RWB says a water use permit is needed to abstract from rivers, lakes, springs and groundwater; irrigation above 1 ha needs a permit while small-scale irrigation under 1 ha, temporary works and households collecting water directly from natural sources without a service provider are exempt; permit requirement depends on the activity, not the volume; irrigation above 10 ha also needs an EIA certificate and feasibility study; decision in 90 days; permits valid 15 years; unpermitted abstraction is an offence (2-3 months and/or FRW 500,000); in recent inspections 83 of 675 users had no valid permit.
title: When is a water abstraction permit required? (Michel Nkurunziza)
notes: Article body read via the AllAfrica copy https://allafrica.com/stories/202608040076.html (the New Times page itself showed only the headline). Secondary summary of LOC-03 and LOC-04; the primary texts govern. It does not address boreholes or livestock watering as standalone categories.

claim: Parliamentary committee asked government to revisit buffer-zone policy for water bodies (session 2025-10-21); the article gives the buffers as 10 m for rivers and 50 m for lakes, says construction is prohibited there, says the Minister of Environment can grant exceptions for tourism-related or specific economic projects, and cites REMA's 2015 figures of 101 lakes, 861 rivers and 860 swamps.
title: MPs call for rethink of buffer for waterbodies as investors' interest grows (Fidele Nsengiyumva)
notes: Policy under review as of Oct 2025: the buffer rules could change. The article does not say what agriculture is allowed inside the buffer.

claim: REMA specified a 50 m buffer zone around all lakes in the country; SMEC prepared lakeshore management guidelines and regulatory recommendations covering Burera, Kivu, Mugesera, Muhazi and Rweru, intended for all 23 lakes in Rwanda; method included GIS mapping, field data and community consultation.
title: Management Guidelines for Lakeshores and Riverbanks in Rwanda
notes: Project page; year not stated (Environment Analyst coverage dates the commission to 2018). The guidelines document itself was not found online [U]; request it from REMA (founder-side, no outreach by this study).

claim: REMA publishes, among its Ministerial Orders, the 2010 lake and river shores order, the Prime Minister's Order of 30/01/2024 on swamplands, the 2021 environmental-audit list order and the list of plains prohibited to construction (files uploaded Aug 2025).
title: Ministerial Orders (REMA resources page, page 1 of 3)
notes: Pages 2 and 3 of the listing were not seen. File upload dates shown on the page, not enactment dates.

title: Source book for the inland fishery resources of Africa, Vol. 1 (lake data tables)

claim: Lake Muhazi: about 37 km long east to west, 0.6-2.0 km wide, catchment about 900 km2 (55% of the Nyabugogo catchment), surface elevation 1,444 m a.s.l., 13 narrow branches; level varies by about 50-70 cm between seasons; June-August inflow is very low; no water shortage for modelled demands.
title: Hydrology of Lake Muhazi and new dyke (presentation, Alsaad Ndayizeye)
organization: Rwanda Water Resources Board (RWB), Water Portal
notes: Workshop slide deck; date taken from the upload folder.

claim: Lake Muhazi is fed by a watershed of about 870 km2, extends roughly 38 km and is drained by the Nyabugogo River; an earth-fill dyke at the outlet is about 225 m long and 4 m high.
title: Muhazi Dyke
notes: Official project page; figures differ slightly from LOC-13 (870 vs about 900 km2; 38 vs 37 km).

claim: Lake Muhazi infobox: area 33 km2, length 37 km, mean depth 10 m, max depth 14 m, catchment 829 km2, surface elevation 1,443 m; western third borders Gasabo (Kigali) and Gicumbi; eastern two-thirds border Rwamagana to the south and Gatsibo and Kayonza to the north; Kigali-Kayonza road runs parallel on the south side; resorts at Gahini and Rwesero; a Rwanda Housing Authority shoreline land-control study around 2014.
